rule_text: An advertisement may not: (1) Include any untrue statement of a material fact, or omit to state a material fact necessary in order to make the statement made, in the light of the circumstances under which it was made, not misleading; (2) Include a material statement of fact that the adviser does not have a reasonable basis for believing it will be able to substantiate upon demand by the Commission; (3) Include information that would reasonably be likely to cause an untrue or misleading implication or inference to be drawn concerning a material fact relating to the investment adviser;
test: Does the copy state material facts (AUM, client numbers, awards, 'no losses') that are untrue, misleading by omission, or that the adviser could not substantiate on demand?
fail_example: Trusted by 1 million investors and never lost a client a dollar.
pass_example: We manage $2.1bn for 3,400 clients as of 31 Dec 2025 (source: Form ADV). Investing involves risk, including loss of principal.

source: SEC Marketing Rule 17 CFR 275.206(4)-1(a)(4); FINRA Rule 2210(d)(1)(D)
rule_text: (4) Discuss any potential benefits to clients or investors connected with or resulting from the investment adviser's services or methods of operation without providing fair and balanced treatment of any material risks or material limitations associated with the potential benefits; ... Members must ensure that statements are clear and not misleading within the context in which they are made, and that they provide balanced treatment of risks and potential benefits.
test: Does the copy promote benefits (income, growth, tax savings, downside protection) without fair and balanced treatment of the material risks and limitations?
fail_example: Our options-income strategy pays you every month, rain or shine.
pass_example: Our options-income strategy seeks monthly income. Income is not guaranteed, and the strategy may limit upside and can lose value in falling markets.

rule_text: No member may make any false, exaggerated, unwarranted, promissory or misleading statement or claim in any communication. ... Communications may not predict or project performance, imply that past performance will recur or make any exaggerated or unwarranted claim, opinion or forecast;
test: Does the copy promise or predict results ('will double', 'guaranteed growth'), imply past performance will repeat, or make exaggerated claims?
fail_example: This fund will return 15% next year - just like it did the last three years.
pass_example: The fund returned 15% in 2025. Past performance does not guarantee future results, and future returns may be lower or negative.

rule_text: (6) Include or exclude performance results, or present performance time periods, in a manner that is not fair and balanced; ... unless the advertisement includes performance results of the same portfolio or composite aggregation for one-, five-, and ten-year periods, each presented with equal prominence and ending on a date that is no less recent than the most recent calendar year-end; except that if the relevant portfolio did not exist for a particular prescribed period, then the life of the portfolio must be substituted for that period.
test: Is performance cherry-picked (best period, best accounts only), or missing 1-, 5- and 10-year (or since-inception) figures shown with equal prominence and ending no earlier than the latest calendar year-end? (Private funds are exempt from the 1/5/10 requirement.)
fail_example: Our growth composite returned 42% from March 2020 to March 2021.
pass_example: Growth composite, net of fees, to 31 Dec 2025: 1-year 8.1%, 5-year 9.4% a year, 10-year 10.2% a year Past performance does not guarantee future results.

rule_text: (1) Any presentation of gross performance, unless the advertisement also presents net performance: (i) With at least equal prominence to, and in a format designed to facilitate comparison with, the gross performance; and (ii) Calculated over the same time period, and using the same type of return and methodology, as the gross performance.
test: If gross (pre-fee) returns appear, is net performance shown with at least equal prominence, for the same period and using the same method?
fail_example: Returns of 11.5% a year (gross of fees).
pass_example: Returns of 11.5% a year gross of fees and 10.3% a year net of fees, for the 5 years to 31 Dec 2025.

rule_text: (6) Any hypothetical performance unless the investment adviser: (i) Adopts and implements policies and procedures reasonably designed to ensure that the hypothetical performance is relevant to the likely financial situation and investment objectives of the intended audience of the advertisement; (ii) Provides sufficient information to enable the intended audience to understand the criteria used and assumptions made in calculating such hypothetical performance; and (iii) Provides (or, if the intended audience is an investor in a private fund, provides, or offers to provide promptly) sufficient information to enable the intended audience to understand the risks and limitations of using such hypothetical performance in making investment decisions;
test: Does the copy show backtested, model, projected or target returns without explaining the assumptions and criteria and the risks and limitations of relying on them (and is it suitable for the intended audience)?
fail_example: Our AI model would have returned 31% a year since 2010.
pass_example: Backtested results (hypothetical, not actual trading) of 9% a year since 2015 assume monthly rebalancing and 0.5% annual costs. Backtests have inherent limitations, including hindsight; actual results will differ.

rule_text: The investment adviser discloses, or reasonably believes that the person giving the testimonial or endorsement discloses, the following at the time the testimonial or endorsement is disseminated: (i) Clearly and prominently: (A) That the testimonial was given by a current client or investor, and the endorsement was given by a person other than a current client or investor, as applicable; (B) That cash or non-cash compensation was provided for the testimonial or endorsement, if applicable; and (C) A brief statement of any material conflicts of interest on the part of the person giving the testimonial or endorsement resulting from the investment adviser's relationship with such person;
test: Is there a testimonial or endorsement (client quote, influencer, 'as seen on') without clear and prominent disclosure of whether the person is a client, whether they were paid, and any material conflict?
fail_example: "Best decision I ever made - they tripled my portfolio!" - @FinanceGuru
pass_example: "Clear advice and quick answers." - Paid endorsement by a non-client who receives a referral fee from us, which creates a conflict of interest.

rule_text: (2) Clearly and prominently discloses, or the investment adviser reasonably believes that the third-party rating clearly and prominently discloses: (i) The date on which the rating was given and the period of time upon which the rating was based; (ii) The identity of the third party that created and tabulated the rating; and (iii) If applicable, that compensation has been provided directly or indirectly by the adviser in connection with obtaining or using the third-party rating.
test: Does the copy cite a rating, ranking or award without stating who gave it, when, the period it covers, and whether the adviser paid for it?
pass_example: Ranked #1 in Example Research's 2025 Adviser Survey (survey period Jan-Jun 2025). We paid a fee to use this ranking.
